commands.author: steipete

target.title: fix(cron): publish removals after durable commit
target.body:
Fixes #104078.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where external cron mirrors could observe a one-shot job as removed before OpenClaw had durably committed that deletion. If the final store write failed, the observer could cancel a wake for a job that still existed on disk, while the live Gateway could temporarily expose the speculative deletion.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Buffer automatic `removed` events for manual runs, normal timer runs, and startup catch-up until the final durable write succeeds.
- Restore the complete live cron topology, durable next-wake snapshot, and catch-up deferral ownership when that write fails.
- Keep the completed deleted-job snapshot for the eventual event, and remove an unreachable invalid-persisted-job deletion branch.
- Document `scheduled` and `removed` hook events as post-commit reconciliation hints.

The change preserves existing `started` and `finished` timing. It does not turn lifecycle hooks into an ordered delta stream; consumers should still reconcile the full durable cron view.

## User Impact

Plugin authors and host integrations can now treat `cron_changed` removal notifications as durable deletion facts. A failed cron-store write emits no removal, and subsequent cron reads continue to expose the still-durable job.

## Evidence

- Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01kx7fqgk4tjw6e9zw6dar21gs`: six new manual, timer, and startup-catch-up success/failure regressions passed.
- Same Testbox: 195 focused cron and Gateway hook tests passed across the new suite, one-shot behavior, startup catch-up, cron ops, timer regressions, and Gateway cron integration.
- Same Testbox: path-scoped `check:changed` passed, including core and test typechecks, lint, import-cycle, database-first storage, and runtime-sidecar guards.
- Source-blind live Gateway proof passed twice with distinct one-shot jobs: each emitted exactly `started` → `finished` → `removed`, the removed snapshot exactly matched the completed job snapshot, and loopback Admin `cron.list` already omitted the job inside the removal callback and afterward.
- Source-blind final-write fault injection was blocked: documented filesystem and SQLite locking surfaces could not safely isolate the deletion commit. The six focused tests provide the deterministic failed-write/no-removal/rollback proof.
- Docs MDX, i18n glossary, and formatting checks passed; targeted oxfmt and `git diff --check` passed.
- Fresh autoreview completed with no accepted/actionable findings (`patch is correct`, 0.93).

Release-note context: automatic cron removals now publish only after durable deletion succeeds and retain the full deleted-job snapshot.

AI-assisted implementation; maintainer-reviewed against current `main`. No agent transcript is included.
